chunks: And from him, from Abdullah ibn Jabalah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"A man has ownership over his brother's son and his brother from breastfeeding (milk-kinship)."

key_terms.أَخَاهُ: His brother; a direct sibling included in the ruling.
key_terms.ابْنَ أَخِيهِ: His brother's son; a specific male relative included in the ruling.
key_terms.الرِّضَاعَةِ: Breastfeeding; refers to milk-kinship (radha'ah) which establishes legal family ties similar to blood relations.
key_terms.يَمْلِكُ: He owns/has authority over; indicates legal possession or dominion.

ai.seo_question: Who does a man have legal ownership or authority over according to this hadith from Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: In the context of manumission (itq) within Shia jurisprudence, this hadith clarifies that a master's partial ownership extends to his brother and paternal nephew, as well as those related through breastfeeding. This ruling underscores the principle that radha'ah (milk-kinship) establishes legal ties equivalent to nasab (bloodline), thereby influencing inheritance and manumission rights. It reflects the practical application of kinship categories in determining the distribution of a freed slave's value among co-owners.
